market.summary: India fell for a third day: the Nifty closed at 22,687.65 (-0.54%) with small caps weaker (-1.1%) and IT one of the worst sectors (-1.4%) after its strong week. Brent jumped about 3% to $112.5 on attacks on a Saudi Aramco field and talk of renewed US-Israel strikes on Iran, and FIIs sold about Rs 3,459 Cr in cash (DIIs bought Rs 2,891 Cr). In New York, chip and AI stocks led a sell-off (Nasdaq about -2.2% by late morning), which is a headwind for HCLTech tomorrow; the regime stays RISK-OFF, so new positions should stay small.

points.text: Sensex 73,249.39 (-460 pts, -0.62%), Nifty 22,687.65 (-123.7 pts, -0.54%); Midcap 100 about -0.9%, Smallcap 100 about -1.1%; Nifty IT -1.4%, Auto -1%, Bank Nifty -0.2%.
Brent up about 3% to $112.5 a barrel after attacks on a Saudi Aramco oilfield; Asian indices closed 2.5-3.5% lower.
NSE provisional cash flows 22 Oct: FIIs net sold about Rs 3,459 Cr, DIIs net bought about Rs 2,891 Cr; FIIs have sold about Rs 7,704 Cr over 5 sessions. Only about 25% of NIFTY 500 stocks rose today.

US at about 11:30 am New York time: S&P 500 -1.3%, Nasdaq -2.2%, VIX up about 14% to 19; chipmakers led the drop on worries that AI infrastructure spending is slowing, and IBM fell after keeping its 2026 growth guidance unchanged. The 10-year yield eased to about 5.0%.
Jio Platforms IPO was subscribed 4.3x by early afternoon on day 2 (QIB 9.8x, retail 1.4x); it closes on 23 Oct.

THELEELA.summary: The transcript of the mid-October results call was filed today. Management guided H2 FY27 EBITDA growth of about 17-19%, expects Q3 RevPAR to grow at a high double-digit rate, and says Q3 is trending very strongly; H2 is usually about 65% of the year. That supports the PEAD drift, but the stock closed at 595.65, under the 604.51 average entry, after falling from 622.75 (19 Oct) to 585.50 (21 Oct), and the weekly RSI is overbought (70.6).

points.text: Q2: operating revenue +33% to Rs 411.9 Cr, room revenue +39%, RevPAR +30%, India occupancy 69% at an average rate of Rs 25,046.
Outlook: H2 FY27 EBITDA growth about 17-19%; Q3 RevPAR high double-digit growth; target Rs 2,000 Cr EBITDA and 5,200+ keys by FY2030.
Net debt Rs 1,215 Cr, 1.4x trailing EBITDA (3.7x in March 2025); borrowing cost cut a further 30 bp from mid-October. Capex about Rs 450 Cr this year, Rs 600 Cr next.
